query: I have a vague product idea. Ask me the hard questions before we commit to building it.
We agreed on the behavior. Turn that shared understanding into a precise feature spec.
I need to plan a migration across several services without losing the existing behavior.
Split this approved spec into independently shippable tracker tickets with dependencies.
Challenge this proposal using our actual repository docs, not assumptions.
Make this UI feel less generic. Improve its typography, spacing, and visual hierarchy.
This CSS animation drops frames and stutters on phones. Find the performance problem.
The app feels slow because everything animates. Remove the unnecessary motion.
Stress-test this interface with empty states, huge numbers, long names, and broken images.
Build several genuinely different UI directions so I can compare them in a live picker.
The implementation is ready. Prove it on the running app, open a PR, and merge it.
We have no real end-to-end verification procedure. Create one that drives the actual app.
Before this change ships, map what else its shared API and configuration could break.
I need a prepared isolated machine to run this build and browser QA, then clean it up.
Model the bad event orders in this concurrent workflow and verify the safety property.
Production broke after the release. Check health and recover through the authorized rollback path.
Audit the security boundaries and find concrete exploitable vulnerabilities in this repository.
An agent has been busy for a long time. Determine whether it is progressing, drifting, or stuck.
We have a confusing dependency API error. Find the official contract before changing our code.
I fixed the same symptom twice and it still fails. Trace the first point where things went wrong.
What do I run after a session to improve things? Review the work and capture durable lessons.
The assistant keeps making the same mistake. Turn the correction into durable guidance.
Find repeated manual work in my sessions and automate the recurring chore.
Audit our tests and remove duplicated checks without losing independent consumer contracts.
Reconsider this whole system from its original vision now that model capabilities have changed.
Explain how this unfamiliar subsystem works and where the important code lives.
Show me a concise visual diagram and code-shape sketch of the architecture we are discussing.
Untangle this codebase so coding agents need less context per change and break fewer things.
Why was this module designed this way? Find the original decisions and their tradeoffs.
Teach me this concept with an explanation that builds real understanding, not a code dump.
